messages:
Incident Bot: PAGER -> tenant-isolation-alert for customer Photon (cust_id=5902) in dedicated-vpc-us-west2. Potential cross-tenant routing observed: 0.8% of requests from tenant-5902 routed to pool-dedicated-phi-03 where tenant-5907 also has active allocations. Severity: P2. Paging oncall.
Oncall Bot: @channel oncall: Priya Kumar is current rotation. Priya, please ack and triage. :rotating_light:
Priya Kumar: acked. Looking. Can someone paste the anomaly query that triggered this? Need sample request ids.
Sanjay Rao: grabbing logs now — running quick hop query against envoy metrics and our routing audit. Will paste results in 2m.
Maya Chen: FYI Photon reported a suspicious user seeing another org's prompt in their logs earlier. They've DM'd Support. Evelyn is on the thread.
Evelyn (PhotonOps): thanks team — our SRE observed one example at 14:07 UTC where an internal prompt snippet referenced tenant-5907. We paused traffic on our side but want full scope.
Sanjay Rao: query output: `SELECT count(*) as hits, dest_pool FROM routed_requests WHERE src_tenant=5902 AND dest_tenant!=5902 GROUP BY dest_pool;` -> small set returned: hits=52 over 10k requests, dest_pool=pool-dedicated-phi-03.
Sanjay Rao: attaching sample request ids: r: 0a3f9b, 7c2e11, 89d4ff — logs show route_key mismatch in router-proxy: `route_bind=phi-03` despite tenant binding header `x-tenant:5902`.
Priya Kumar: thanks. First step — isolate impact and reduce blast radius. Recommendation: temporarily withdraw tenant-5902 from pool-dedicated-phi-03 routing via live-routing policy; also mark pool-dedicated-phi-03 as quarantined for cross-tenant audit. Who can run the routing change? Maya?
Maya Chen: I can execute. Plan: apply canary routing rule to force tenant-5902 -> pool-fallback-ephemeral-01. Rolling change will be immediate for new sessions. Do we want to evict existing connections/kv caches? That affects inflight latency.
Carlos Diaz: If we evict connections we risk disrupting long-running streams. Alternative: leave inflight sessions, but scrub KV prefix caches on phi-03 for tenant-5902 keys. We have an admin command: `rdwctl cache flush --pool=phi-03 --tenant=5902 --prefix=tenant:5902`.
Priya Kumar: good call. Start with routing redirect for new sessions + cache flush on phi-03. Eviction only if cross-reads continue. Also enable detailed tracing for dest_pool phi-03 for next 30m.
Maya Chen: executing routing change now — applying policy:
```
# routing policy patch
patch: {
  match: { tenant: "5902" }
  action: { route_to: "pool-fallback-ephemeral-01", rollout: immediate }
}
```
Maya Chen: policy applied. New sessions should go to fallback pool. Confirming with health checks.
Oncall Bot: Deploy event recorded: routing-policy/patch by maya.rolling-id=rp-1716490247.
Sanjay Rao: started cache flush on phi-03 for tenant 5902: command issued.
Sanjay Rao: logs from cache flush:
```
INFO: flushing keys for tenant:5902 on pool:phi-03
deleted 178 keys (kv-layer)
deleted 3 persistent entries (prefix-logs)
```
Priya Kumar: good. Now enable intensive packet and request tracing on phi-03 for correlation ids matching sample list. Sanjay, set log level to debug for router-proxy on phi-03.
Sanjay Rao: done — `router-proxy` debug on phi-03. Pushing temporary retention to 1h for those traces.
Evelyn (PhotonOps): appreciate the fast action. Two Qs from Photon security: 1) did any customer data surface in the wrong tenant's logs? 2) what's the window of exposure?
Priya Kumar: preliminary: 52 cross-routed requests over ~12 minutes between 14:05-14:17 UTC. We have samples and will do payload-level inspection under NDA. At first glance, payload snippets are small (prompt prefixes) not full data dumps. But we need to confirm.
Carlos Diaz: starting payload audit on stored request logs. Will scrub any PII before sharing. If we find anything > minimal exposure we'll follow customer-notification playbook.
Maya Chen: phi-03 has been quarantined for new allocations. Eviction not yet performed. Recommend 30m observation window after cache flush. If cross-reads drop to zero, we'll keep quarantine and run a full routing config audit.
Priya Kumar: Agreed. Also we need to check control-plane broadcast events — any config push to routing mesh around 14:04 that could cause stale bindings?
Sanjay Rao: checking gitops and control-plane logs. There was a config-sync job at 14:02 UTC from infra-deploy pipeline but it was a benign security patch; no routing edits in that PR. However one of the mesh agents reported a delayed heartbeat at 14:03 — could be related.
Priya Kumar: mark as action item: Sanjay to collect mesh agent heartbeats + config hash diff for phi-03 between 13:55-14:10.
Sanjay Rao: on it.
Evelyn (PhotonOps): Photon needs ETA on remediation and whether they'll have to rotate keys or do anything on their side.
Priya Kumar: immediate ask for Photon: rotate any short-lived cached tokens if concerned, but we will do internal audit first. We'll update with scope and remediation plan within 2 hours. For now, no mass rotation required unless we find payloads with secrets.
Carlos Diaz: audit update: initial scan of payloads shows 6 requests with user-supplied prompts containing email-like strings. Marked for deeper review. I'm redacting and will escalate if anything obvious.
Maya Chen: next step timeline: 00-05m: routing change + cache flush (done). 05-35m: tracing + payload audit (in progress). 35-60m: decision point — if cross-reads=0 continue quarantine & start root cause. If cross-reads persist, escalate to eviction and failover for phi-03.
Priya Kumar: assigning tasks: Sanjay - mesh heartbeats + control-plane diffs. Carlos - payload audit and prepare summary for legal/comms. Maya - keep quarantine + monitor routing metrics. I'll coordinate customer comms and decide on eviction cutoff.
Incident Bot: reminder: create incident doc in /incidents with tag tenant-isolation and link this thread.
Priya Kumar: creating incident doc now. Also pinging Trust & Safety and Legal for notification threshold.
Maya Chen: metric check: after routing change + flush, cross-tenant hits in the last 5m = 1 (sampling noise). Previously 52. Flapping? Need tracing.
Sanjay Rao: collected mesh agent heartbeat dump and control-plane diffs, attaching hashes: `config@13:55 -> hash=a1f3`, `config@14:05 -> hash=a1f3` (no change). Mesh agent phi-03 reported queue delay at 14:03 for ~22s — possibly replayed a stale route-binding during that window.
Priya Kumar: that'd explain a small window of wrong route resolution. Likely not a config spew, more ephemeral mesh routing inconsistency. Still treat as bug.
Evelyn (PhotonOps): Photon confirm they saw exactly the 14:07 occurrence and not widespread. Thank you. We'll stand by for the payload audit result.
Carlos Diaz: payload audit: after redaction, no high-sensitivity secrets observed so far. The 6 suspicious requests contained emails and short PII fragments; none contained full documents or API keys. Marking as low-sev for now. Will push final report in 45m.
Priya Kumar: good. Next: schedule a postmortem cause timeline analysis and add remediation: 1) more robust route-binding atomicity in mesh; 2) add per-tenant KV prefix isolation checks during routing decisions; 3) retroactive scan for similar small spikes in other pools over last 7d.
Maya Chen: opening remediation issue now and assigning to eng-runtime and eng-infra.
Oncall Bot: status update reminder in 30m. If cross-reads persist at cutoff (1716492000), we'll escalate to pool-eviction.
Priya Kumar: closing immediate loop — routing redirect + cache flush done, tracing + payload audit in progress. Customer notified (PhotonOps). Will update thread with final audit and chosen remediation. Thanks team. :heavy_check_mark:
Evelyn (PhotonOps): thanks everyone. Please include confirmation when phi-03 is safe for normal allocations.
Carlos Diaz: will confirm in final report.
Priya Kumar: final note — add H/T links and sample ids to incident doc for compliance.
